questions.stem: Why does a potometer actually measure water uptake rather than transpiration directly?

options.text: Because the potometer cannot detect water vapour
Because some water taken up is used in photosynthesis, not all is transpired
Because the potometer only works in bright light
Because transpiration only happens at night

questions.explanation: A potometer measures total water uptake, but a small amount of this water is used in photosynthesis and other metabolic processes rather than being transpired. However, since about 99% is transpired, it is a close estimate.
